paragraphs: Carlisle Companies Incorporated ("Carlisle," the "Company," "we," "us" or "our") is a leading supplier of innovative building envelope products and solutions for more energy-efficient buildings. Through our building products businesses, Carlisle Construction Materials and Carlisle Weatherproofing Technologies, and family of leading brands, Carlisle delivers innovative, labor reducing and environmentally responsible products and solutions to customers through the Carlisle Experience.

Our Company website is www.carlisle.com, through which we make available, free of charge, our Annual Report on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and Current Reports on Form 8-K and all amendments to those reports, as soon as reasonably practicable after these reports are electronically filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). Information on, or that can be accessed through, our website is not incorporated by reference and should not be considered part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. All references to "Notes" refer to our Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We strive to be a leading manufacturer and supplier of innovative building envelope products and solutions that make buildings more energy-efficient in the markets we serve. Vision 2030, our strategic plan, builds on Carlisle's track record of success and our pivot to a pure play building products portfolio, leveraging mega trends around energy-efficiency, labor-savings, and the re-roofing cycle, to generate above market growth driven by innovation, the Carlisle Experience, and the Carlisle Operating System ("COS").

The key pillars of Vision 2030 are well-ingrained throughout the Company and guide our value-creating strategy. They include (1) driving above market organic revenue growth through continued investment in innovation, (2) maintaining best-in-class production, service, and delivery capabilities to provide the Carlisle Experience to our customers, (3) using COS, an operating structure and strategy deployment system based on lean enterprise and six sigma principles, to consistently drive efficiencies and operating leverage, (4) building scale with synergistic acquisitions, (5) continuing to invest in and develop exceptional talent, and (6) maintaining a balanced, returns-focused approach to capital deployment which includes returning excess capital to stockholders.

COS is a continuous improvement process that defines the way we do business and is deeply embedded in our culture throughout Carlisle's operations. Waste is eliminated and efficiencies are improved enterprise-wide, driving both improvements to our sustainability efforts by reducing our carbon footprint and increasing profitability. These efforts expand beyond production areas, as COS drives new product innovation, engineering, supply chain management, warranty and product rationalization.

As demand accelerates for energy-efficient solutions for the sustainable buildings of the future, we will continue to emphasize the development of energy-efficient products, systems, and solutions for the roof and throughout the building envelope that reduce carbon emissions from the built environment which is estimated to contribute as much as 30% of annual greenhouse gas ("GHG") emissions.

We intend to continue to seek synergistic acquisitions that will enhance our ability to service our customers with a broader set of energy-efficient solutions. Refer to Note 3 for further discussion of acquisitions made during the past three years.

We believe our proactive approach to continuous improvement initiatives and focus on delivering the Carlisle Experience to our customers enables us to maintain resilient margins. We remain focused on continuing our value-creating journey with the proven foundational pillars of Vision 2030 ingrained in our Carlisle culture of continuous improvement and returns-focused capital deployment.

The CCM segment has evolved from a supplier of the first single-ply ethylene propylene diene monomer ("EPDM") roofing membranes in the early 1960s to today, where we deliver innovative, easy-to-install and energy-efficient solutions through the Carlisle Experience for customers who are creating the sustainable buildings of the future. CCM is a manufacturer and supplier of premium roofing products and related technologies primarily for the commercial construction market. CCM offers high-performance, single-ply roofing solutions that include EPDM, thermoplastic polyolefin ("TPO"), polyvinyl chloride ("PVC"), architectural metal and roof garden systems.

EPDM, TPO and PVC membrane and polyisocyanurate ("polyiso") insulation are sold together in warranted systems or separately in non-warranted systems to the new construction, repair and replacement, and general construction markets. These products are primarily sold under the Carlisle SynTec, Versico, Weatherbond and Hunter Panels brands in the United States of America ("U.S." or "United States") and throughout the world, and EPDM membranes under the Resitrix and Hertalan brands primarily in Europe.

CCM operates manufacturing facilities located throughout the United States, its primary market, and in Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom ("U.K.") and Romania. The majority of CCM's products are sold through a network of authorized sales representatives and distributors in North America and Europe.

Key raw materials for this segment include methylene diphenyl diisocyanate ("MDI"), polyol, EPDM polymer, TPO polymer, carbon black and coated steel. These raw materials generally have at least two vendor sources. The vendor typically has multiple processing facilities for key raw materials that are single sourced.
Revenues and earnings for CCM have historically been higher in the second and third quarters due to increased construction activity during those periods from favorable weather conditions.

CCM serves a large and diverse customer base; however, in 2025 CCM's two largest customers represented 33% of the Company's consolidated revenues. The loss of either of these customers could have a material adverse effect on the Company's consolidated revenues and operating income. Both of these customers' business is covered under a number of independent local agreements.

paragraphs: The Company's business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows can be affected by a number of factors, including those material factors set forth below, those set forth in our "Forward Looking Statements" disclosure in Item 7 and those set forth elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, any one of which could cause the Company's actual results to vary materially from recent results or from anticipated future results and make an investment in the Company speculative or risky.

A key pillar of the Company's Vision 2030 strategic plan is building scale with synergistic acquisitions. When companies become available for purchase, the process is often highly competitive, which tends to result in relatively high valuations for the target company. There can be no assurance that the Company will be able to continue to identify, negotiate and finance suitable acquisitions at values the Company considers reasonable.

Acquisitions involve numerous risks, including the failure to realize expected revenue growth and/or operating and cost synergies from integration initiatives, an increased dependency on the markets served, the diversion of management's attention from its existing operations or increased debt to finance the acquisitions. The successful realization of revenue growth, cost reductions and synergies and increases in profitability overall are dependent upon successful integration initiatives. If these integration initiatives are not fully realized, there may be a negative effect on the Company's business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows, including goodwill and/or intangible asset impairments, which may be material.

The loss of, a significant decline in business with, or pricing pressure from, one or more of the Company's key customers could adversely affect the Company's business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.

The Company's CCM segment operates in several niche markets in which a large portion of the segment's revenues are attributable to a few large customers. These markets have experienced recent consolidation among distributors of roofing materials and complementary building products. A significant reduction in purchases by one or more of these customers could have an adverse effect on the business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows of one or more of the Company's segments.

Some of the Company's key customers enjoy significant purchasing power that may be used to exert pricing pressure on the Company. Additionally, as many of the Company's businesses are part of a long supply chain to the ultimate consumer, the Company's business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows could be adversely affected if one or more key customers elects to in-source or find alternative suppliers for the production of a product or products that the Company currently provides.

paragraphs: Throughout 2025, despite continued headwinds in new construction and a complex economic environment, we continued to execute against our Vision 2030 strategy, and we remain very confident in our ability to achieve our Vision 2030 financial objectives. Over the course of the year, we made progress on all our key pillars of Vision 2030. We increased investments in innovation to develop new market-leading products. We enhanced our emphasis on the Carlisle Operating System ("COS") and expanded automation in our factories to drive operational excellence. We added significant management talent and further elevated the Carlisle Experience to strengthen customer loyalty and service. And above all else, we continued to deliver on our commitment to being superior capital allocators.

Carlisle's performance during 2025 adds to our history of resilience through the economic cycles and challenges we have faced over the years, such as the Covid pandemic. We delivered another solid year of cash flow, generating over $1 billion of operating cash flow, which continued to provide balance sheet optionality. As the M&A environment in 2025 was challenging, we turned a significant portion of that cash flow to share repurchases, as we continued to see this as a solid opportunity for capital deployment.

At CCM, solid re-roofing demand, which represents approximately 70% of our commercial roofing business, continued to help stabilize our business as new construction markets work through the bottom of the cycle. At CWT, our recent acquisitions and operational initiatives contributed to revenue growth, and we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing need for energy-efficient weatherproofing solutions.

North America is the most attractive building-products market globally, supported by strong, long-term fundamentals including the demand for energy-efficient solutions, the need to improve labor productivity, and the recurring maintenance requirements of an aging non-residential building stock—over 70% of which is more than 25 years old. Buildings are a critical and indispensable component of the physical economy. They must be built, maintained, and continuously improved. This structural reality reinforces the durability and necessity of our end markets.

Carlisle's imperative business continues to benefit from a strong re-roofing market, and we continued to benefit from our position as a North American leader in the world's largest building-products market. Carlisle's leadership position in this essential market, highly responsive cost structure combined with the discipline of COS and our proven capital allocation framework, continues to translate into superior and sustainable margin performance.

While we expect the current challenging market conditions to continue into the first half of 2026, our solid financial position, robust cash flow, and ongoing commitment to operational excellence enable us to continue generating strong returns, pursue value-enhancing acquisitions, and deliver shareholder value.

Carlisle Companies Incorporated ("Carlisle," the "Company," "we," "us" or "our") 為創新建築包覆產品與解決方案的主要供應商，專注於提供更節能的建築物解決方案。透過我們的建築產品業務 Carlisle Construction Materials 和 Carlisle Weatherproofing Technologies，以及 Carlisle 的領導品牌家族，Carlisle 透過 Carlisle Experience 向客戶提供創新、節省人力且負責任的產品與解決方案。

本公司網站為 www.carlisle.com，透過該網站，我們免費提供年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）與現況報告（Form 8-K）以及所有這些報告的更正版本，於這些報告電子提交或提供給證券交易委員會（"SEC"）後儘速提供。本公司網站上的資訊或可透過該網站存取的資訊，並未被納入參考，亦不應視為本年度報告（Form 10-K）的一部分。所有提及 "Notes" 均指本年度報告（Form 10-K）中 "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements" 的附註。

我們致力於成為創新建築包覆產品與解決方案的主要製造商與供應商，以使我們服務的市場中的建築物更具節能效果。Vision 2030 為我們的戰略計畫，建立在 Carlisle 過往成功經驗之上，並轉向純粹的建築產品組合，利用能源效率、節省人力及重新鋪設屋頂週期等宏觀趨勢，以創新、Carlisle Experience 以及 Carlisle Operating System（"COS"）推動超越市場的成長。

Vision 2030 的關鍵支柱已深植於本公司之中，並引導我們的價值創造策略。這些支柱包括（1）透過持續投資創新，推動超越市場的內生營收成長；（2）維持最佳等級的生產、服務與交付能力，以提供 Carlisle Experience 給客戶；（3）透過 COS，一種基於精益企業與六西格瑪原則的運營結構與策略落實系統，持續推動效率與營運槓桿；（4）透過協同效應的併購建立規模；（5）持續投資並發展卓越人才；（6）維持平衡、以回報為導向的資本運用方式，包括將過度資本回饋給股東。
COS 是一種持續改進的流程，定義了我們的作業方式，並深植於 Carlisle 的文化之中。透過 COS，我們消除浪費並提升企業整體的效率，同時推動永續發展努力，減少碳足跡並提高利潤率。這些努力不僅限於生產領域，COS 還推動新產品創新、工程、供應鏈管理、保証與產品精簡。
隨著對未來永續建築物節能解決方案的需求加速成長，我們將持續強調開發節能產品、系統與解決方案，以減少建築環境的碳排放，據估計，建築環境的碳排放佔年度溫室氣體（"GHG"）排放量的高達 30%。
我們意圖持續尋求能提升我們服務客戶能力的協同效應併購，以提供更廣泛的節能解決方案。有關過去三年所進行的併購，請參閱附註 3。
我們相信，我們對持續改進計畫的積極態度，以及專注於為客戶提供 Carlisle Experience 的努力，使我們能維持強韌的毛利率。我們持續專注於價值創造的旅程，並以 Vision 2030 的已證實基礎支柱深植於 Carlisle 的持續改進文化與以回報為導向的資本運用方式。

CCM 應報告分部從1960年代初期作為第一款單層乙丙橡膠（"EPDM"）屋頂隔熱膜供應商，進步到今天，本公司透過 Carlisle Experience 提供創新、易安裝且節能的解決方案，服務正在打造未來永續建築的客戶。CCM 是一家製造與供應高階屋頂產品及相關技術的公司，主要服務商業建築市場。CCM 提供高性能的單層屋頂解決方案，包括 EPDM、熱塑性聚烯烴（"TPO"）、聚氯乙烯（"PVC"）、建築用金屬及屋頂花園系統。

EPDM、TPO 及 PVC 隔熱膜與聚異氰尿酸酯（"polyiso"）絕熱材料，會一起銷售於有保證系統，或分開銷售於無保證系統，服務新建造、修繕與更換及一般建造市場。這些產品主要以 Carlisle SynTec、Versico、Weatherbond 及 Hunter Panels 品牌銷售於美國（"U.S." 或 "United States"）及全球各地，EPDM 隔熱膜則以 Resitrix 及 Hertalan 品牌主要銷售於歐洲。
CCM 在美國，其主要市場，以及德國、荷蘭、英國（"U.K."）及羅馬尼亞設有製造廠。CCM 的大多數產品透過北美及歐洲的授權銷售代表及經銷商網路銷售。
此應報告分部的主要原材料包括甲苯二苯基二異氰酸酯（"MDI"）、聚醚、EPDM 樹脂、TPO 樹脂、碳黑及塗層鋼鐵。這些原材料通常至少有兩家供應商。供應商通常對關鍵原材料有數個加工廠，這些原材料為單一來源。
CCM 的營收與獲利歷來在第二及第三季較高，因該期間因天氣條件良好，建造活動增加。
CCM 服務廣大且多樣化的客戶羣；然而，在2025年，CCM 的兩大客戶佔本公司合併營收的33%。失去其中任一客戶，可能對本公司合併營收及營運獲利產生重大不利影響。這兩家客戶的業務均受多項獨立當地協議所覆蓋。

paragraphs: 2025 年全年，儘管新興建設持續面臨挑戰，且總體經濟環境複雜，我們仍持續執行 Vision 2030 策略，並對達成 Vision 2030 財務目標的能力建立高度信心。在本年度中，我們在 Vision 2030 的所有關鍵支柱上都取得進展。我們增加對創新投資，以開發市場領先的產品。我們強化對 Carlisle Operating System ("COS") 的重視，並擴大工廠自動化，以推動作業卓越。我們增加重要的管理人才，並進一步提升 Carlisle Experience，以強化客戶忠誠度與服務。最重要的是，我們持續履行對成為優秀資本配置者的承諾。
Carlisle 在 2025 年的表現，再次展現我們在經濟週期與多年來所面對的挑戰（例如 Covid 疫情）中展現的韌性。我們又度過一個穩健的現金流年，產生超過 10 億美元的營運現金流，持續為資產負債表提供選擇性。2025 年的併購環境具有挑戰性，因此我們將相當大一部分現金流用於股票回購，因為我們持續認為這是資本配置的優良機會。
在 CCM，穩健的重新鋪蓋需求，代表約 70% 的商業屋頂業務，持續幫助穩定我們的業務，因新建市場正在經歷週期底部。在 CWT，我們最近的收購與作業計畫促進營收成長，我們已處於有利位置，以把握對能源效率天氣防護解決方案日益增長的需求。
北美是全球最具吸引力的建築產品市場，這是由強勁且長期的基本面所支撐，包括對能源效率解決方案的需求、改善勞動生產力的需要，以及非住宅建築存量的持續維護需求—其中超過 70% 的建築物已超過 25 年。建築物是實體經濟中至關重要且不可或缺的零組件。它們必須被建造、維護並持續改善。這種結構性現實強化了我們終端市場的耐用性與必要性。
Carlisle 的核心業務持續受益於強勁的重新鋪蓋市場，我們也持續受益於我們在全球最大建築產品市場中北美領導者的地位。Carlisle 在這個關鍵市場的領導地位，加上高度靈活的成本結構與 COS 的紀律性，以及我們已證實的資本配置架構，持續轉化為優越且可持續的毛利率表現。
雖然我們預期目前困難的市場環境會持續至 2026 年上半年，但我們穩健的財務狀況、強勁的現金流與持續對作業卓越的承諾，使我們能夠繼續產生強勁回報、追求價值提升的收購，並為股東創造價值。

paragraphs: 本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流可能受多種因素影響，包括下列重要因素、本年度報告表 10-K 第 7 項所載之「未來展望陳述」揭露內容，以及本年度報告表 10-K 其他地方所載之因素，任何一項因素均可能導致本公司實際結果與近期結果或預期未來結果有重大差異，並使投資本公司成為一種投機或風險性行為。
本公司 Vision 2030 戰略計劃的重要支柱之一是透過具有協同效益的收購來擴大規模。當有公司可供收購時，這個過程通常非常競爭，往往導致目標公司的估值相對較高。本公司無法保證將持續識別、協商並籌資適合的收購案，且價值符合本公司認為合理。
收購涉及多種風險，包括未能實現預期的收入成長及/或透過整合計畫所產生的營運與成本協同效益、對所服務市場的依賴度增加、管理階層的注意力被分散至現有營運，或因收購而增加債務。收入成長、成本削減及協同效益的實現，以及整體獲利能力的提升，均依賴整合計畫的成功執行。若這些整合計畫未能完全實現，可能會對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流產生負面影響，包括商譽及/或無形資產減損，此等影響可能為重大。
本公司與任一關鍵客戶之關係中斷、與任一關鍵客戶之業務大幅減少，或任一關鍵客戶對本公司施加價格壓力，均可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流產生不利影響。
本公司 CCM 分部經營於多個利基市場，其中分部之收入有相當大一部分來自少數大型客戶。這些市場近期經歷了屋頂材料及補充建築產品經銷商的合併。若任一或數個這些客戶之採購量大幅減少，可能對本公司一個或多個分部之業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流產生不利影響。
本公司部分關鍵客戶擁有顯著的採購力，可能用以對本公司施加價格壓力。此外，因本公司許多業務為最終消費者長鏈供應鏈中的一環，若任一或數個關鍵客戶決定將目前由本公司提供的產品或產品之生產內製化，或尋找替代供應商，則可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流產生不利影響。
